The invention relates to a portable device for performing video electroencephalography. The device is designed to enable the acquisition of electroencephalographic signals while simultaneously recording video images of the subject, in a compact and easily transportable configuration.

The device comprises a helmet structure intended to be worn on the head of a subject. The helmet structure is formed by a plurality of movable arcuate arms connected to a central portion. These arcuate arms define a support framework that can be positioned around the subject’s head and adjusted to accommodate different head shapes and sizes.

Each arcuate arm is configured to support one or more electrodes. The electrodes are arranged to contact selected areas of the subject’s scalp in order to acquire electroencephalographic signals. The electrodes are connected to an electronic central unit mounted on the helmet structure, which receives and processes the signals detected by the electrodes. The electronic central unit may also store, transmit, or otherwise manage the acquired data.

The device further comprises a video camera mounted on a supporting member. The camera is positioned so as to face the helmet structure, thereby allowing video recording of the subject during electroencephalographic monitoring. This enables correlation between recorded brain activity and visible movements, behavior, or clinical events of the subject.

The arcuate arms of the helmet structure are movable relative to the central portion. In particular, the arms are configured to pivot about different axes, allowing adjustment of the helmet in both longitudinal and frontal directions. This pivoting arrangement improves the adaptability of the device, making it possible to correctly position the electrodes on the scalp while maintaining comfort for the subject.

As a result, the invention provides a portable and adjustable video electroencephalography device that integrates electrode support, signal acquisition electronics, and video recording in a single compact system.
outputs.L4:
A portable video electroencephalography device is provided for recording brain electrical activity while simultaneously obtaining video images of the subject. The device includes a helmet-like support structure intended to be worn on the head of a patient. This support structure is formed around a central portion from which a plurality of movable arcuate arms extend. The arms are shaped to follow the contour of the head and are arranged so that the device can be positioned securely and comfortably on users having different head sizes and shapes.

The helmet structure includes longitudinal arms and frontal arms, each of which is connected to the central portion by pivoting joints. These joints allow movement about multiple axes, enabling the arms to be adjusted in different directions. As a result, the helmet can be expanded, contracted, tilted, or otherwise adapted to fit closely against the scalp. This adjustability helps maintain proper electrode contact during use, improving the reliability of electroencephalographic measurements while allowing the patient a degree of mobility.

A plurality of electrodes is mounted on or associated with the arcuate arms. The electrodes are positioned so that, when the helmet is worn, they contact selected regions of the scalp for detecting electrical signals generated by the brain. The electrodes are electrically connected to an electronic unit carried by the device. This onboard electronic unit may include circuitry for receiving, amplifying, filtering, processing, storing, and/or transmitting the EEG signals. By incorporating the electronics directly into the wearable structure, the need for bulky external equipment and long connecting cables can be reduced.

The device further includes a camera mounted so as to face the helmet and the wearer. The camera is arranged to capture video images during EEG recording, allowing patient behavior, movements, facial expressions, and possible seizure-related events to be correlated with the recorded electrical brain activity. The integration of video capture with EEG acquisition provides a compact video-EEG monitoring system that may be used in clinical, ambulatory, or home-monitoring environments.

A key feature of the device is the multi-axis pivoting arrangement of the longitudinal and frontal arcuate arms. This arrangement provides a highly adaptable helmet configuration that can be fitted quickly and accurately to a patient’s head. It also supports stable electrode placement and improved comfort during extended monitoring sessions. By combining adjustable mechanical support, integrated electrodes, onboard electronics, and a forward-facing camera, the device offers a compact and portable solution for video electroencephalography monitoring.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest words in the English language, but it is also one of the most important. It is called a definite article, and it helps us talk about specific people, places, objects, or ideas. For example, when we say “the book,” we are not talking about just any book—we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

This simple word gives clarity and direction to a sentence. Without “the,” many sentences would sound unclear or incomplete. Compare “I saw dog” with “I saw the dog.” The second sentence feels natural because “the” tells us that the dog is specific or already known.

“The” is also used with unique things, such as “the sun,” “the moon,” and “the Earth.” Since there is only one of each in our everyday experience, the word helps identify them as special and definite.

Although “the” is short, it plays a major role in communication. It makes language more precise, helps organize meaning, and connects speakers through shared understanding. In many ways, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have a big impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a portable video EEG device with a helmet structure made of movable arcuate arms, electrode mounts, a central electronics unit, and a camera on a support facing the helmet.
counterfactuals.output: A portable video electroencephalography (EEG) device includes a wearable helmet structure configured to be positioned on a subject’s head and formed from a plurality of movable arcuate arms. The arcuate arms are adjustable relative to one another to conform to different head sizes and shapes and include electrode mounts for positioning EEG electrodes at selected scalp locations. A central electronics unit is coupled to the helmet structure and is configured to receive EEG signals from the electrodes, process and/or store the EEG signals, and communicate the EEG signals to an external device. A camera is mounted on a support positioned to face the helmet structure and is configured to capture video of the subject during EEG monitoring. The device thereby provides portable, integrated acquisition of synchronized video and EEG data while facilitating rapid fitting and stable electrode placement.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise description of an invention relating to a portable device for video electroencephalography, including four pivoting arms extending in longitudinal and front directions and configured to carry EEG electrodes.
counterfactuals.output: A portable device for video electroencephalography is disclosed. The device includes a wearable support frame configured to be positioned on a patient’s head and to support one or more video capture components for recording patient activity during EEG monitoring. The support frame includes four pivoting arms, with at least two arms extending generally in a longitudinal direction and at least two arms extending generally in a front direction. The pivoting arms are adjustable relative to the support frame to accommodate different head sizes and electrode-placement positions. Each arm is configured to carry one or more EEG electrodes and to maintain the electrodes in contact with the patient’s scalp during use. The device enables integrated, portable acquisition of synchronized video and EEG signals without requiring a fixed clinical recording setup.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a portable video electroencephalography apparatus where first and second arms pivot about axes parallel to a front direction, third and fourth arms pivot about axes parallel to a longitudinal direction, and all arms form a patient-worn helmet.
counterfactuals.output:
A portable video electroencephalography (video-EEG) apparatus may include a patient-worn helmet structure configured to support EEG electrodes and associated recording or video components while allowing adjustment to a patient’s head.

The helmet can include a frame having multiple articulated arms:

- A first arm and a second arm are mounted so that each pivots about a respective pivot axis that is parallel to a front direction of the helmet. These arms may swing laterally or vertically relative to the patient’s head to fit different head shapes or to position electrodes.

- A third arm and a fourth arm are mounted so that each pivots about a respective pivot axis that is parallel to a longitudinal direction of the helmet, such as a front-to-back direction extending from the patient’s forehead toward the back of the head. These arms may pivot to conform to the curvature of the skull or to position additional EEG electrodes.

Together, the first, second, third, and fourth arms define a helmet-like support that is worn on the patient’s head. The arms may carry EEG electrodes, electrode leads, sensor mounts, or video-related components, and may be adjustable so the apparatus can be fitted securely and comfortably without requiring a fixed clinical installation. The device is portable, allowing video-EEG monitoring while the patient is ambulatory or located outside a conventional EEG laboratory.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an invention disclosure paragraph for a portable video EEG device with adjustable arcuate arms connected to a central portion, electrode mounting points, an onboard central unit, and an external support member carrying a camera aimed at the helmet.
counterfactuals.output: The invention relates to a portable video electroencephalography (EEG) system configured for ambulatory or bedside neurological monitoring. In one embodiment, the system comprises a helmet-like EEG support structure having a central portion and a plurality of adjustable arcuate arms extending from or coupled to the central portion, the arcuate arms being positionable to conform to different head sizes and shapes. The arcuate arms include a plurality of electrode mounting points configured to receive, retain, and position EEG electrodes at selected locations on a subject’s scalp. An onboard central unit is carried by the helmet structure and is operatively connected to the electrodes for receiving EEG signals, performing signal conditioning, storing data, transmitting data wirelessly or through a wired connection, and/or providing power management for the device. The system further includes an external support member, such as a stand, boom, bracket, or wearable frame, carrying a camera oriented toward the helmet and the subject’s head to acquire video data synchronized with the EEG data. The camera may be positioned to capture subject movement, electrode placement, and clinical events during monitoring, thereby enabling integrated portable video EEG recording without requiring a fixed clinical installation.
